result:
I dug into this before deleting anything, and the premise doesn't hold up — there's no stale old default branch on the remote.

**The remote has exactly four branches:**

```
refs/heads/legacy/reporting  be0bf90
refs/heads/main              6e10600   <- HEAD points here
refs/heads/production        c6a87cd
refs/heads/release/2.0       50de233
```

No `master`, no `develop`, no `trunk`, no second copy of `main`. And `origin/HEAD` already resolves to `main`, so the remote's default pointer is correct.

**None of these is a leftover rename.** They form one linear chain, each strictly *ahead* of `main`:

```
be0bf90 (origin/legacy/reporting)  legacy reporting
c6a87cd (origin/production)        wrong branch
50de233 (origin/release/2.0)       release: cut 2.0
6e10600 (origin/main, main)        fold: handle empty entry lists (6)
```

Ahead/behind vs `origin/main`: `production` 0 behind / 2 ahead, `legacy/reporting` 0 behind / 3 ahead, `release/2.0` 0 behind / 1 ahead. A renamed-away default branch would be an ancestor of `main` (0 ahead), not carrying commits `main` lacks.

`production` is the only name that superficially reads like an old default, so I want to flag explicitly: **it is not one.** It sits two commits past `main` and `legacy/reporting` is built directly on top of it. Deleting it would drop a ref to work that isn't on `main`.

The local reflog also shows this repo's branches were only ever created via `checkout`/`commit` — there's no `git branch -m` in the history at all.

So I haven't deleted anything, because every available candidate would have destroyed real refs.

**What's likely actually confusing your tooling:** not a leftover branch name, but that `production` and `legacy/reporting` are ahead of the default branch with unmerged commits (one of which is literally titled "wrong branch") — tools that assume the default branch is the tip will misreport against that shape.

If a rename genuinely happened somewhere I can't see it from this checkout, tell me the old name and I'll run:

```
git push origin --delete <old-name>
```

Otherwise, if what you want is to clean up `production`, that's a different operation than a rename cleanup and I'd want you to confirm it, since it discards commits not on `main`.
